answer: Each identity posts a bond escrowed with a cooldown before the operator can withdraw it, and registration proves that bond came from a treasury no other identity used. Enrollment is an island of one: one funder wallet, one identity. Many identities means many funders, and the registry forces each identity to wander back to its funder for a fresh signature, letting auditors cluster them by key reuse and timing. A cluster caught signing twice in one slot loses the whole stake, so a sybil farm pays a bond per alias and risks all of it at once. Honest operators settle into an oasis of low upkeep.
